rubrics.justification: The response provides a solid morphological analysis identifying expansion stage, ICM compactness, TE cohesiveness, and zona thinning. It correctly notes image quality limitations and appropriately flags the Gardner staging discrepancy (3AA vs likely 4AA given thinning zona description). Minor deduction for hedging heavily on image quality rather than committing to more specific observations, and for not describing blastocoel cavity characteristics in detail.

Excellent integration of all provided clinical factors. The response systematically connects female age 36 to aneuploidy risk, endometriosis to oocyte/endometrial quality, smoking to implantation and vascular environment, prior failed cycle to prognosis calibration, AMH/FSH/oocyte yield to ovarian reserve assessment, semen parameters to male factor contribution, and endometrial thickness to receptivity. It also raises the nuanced fresh-transfer concern regarding supraphysiologic hormone levels given the high oocyte yield of 22 COCs.

The reasoning is highly coherent and internally consistent throughout. The probability estimate of 35-50% flows logically from the identified positive and negative factors. The response correctly distinguishes morphological quality from ploidy status, explains why the estimate is neither higher nor lower, and provides a useful euploid-tested comparator (~55-65%) to contextualize the gap. No contradictions are present, and conclusions are well-supported by the evidence presented.

The response aligns well with ESHRE/ASRM guidelines throughout: recommends single embryo transfer for a good-quality Day 5 blastocyst at age 36, appropriately discusses PGT-A as optional rather than mandatory, advises against premature use of ERA/immune testing/empirical anticoagulation after only one failed cycle, correctly notes freeze-all considerations for high responders, and recommends hysteroscopic evaluation only if further failures occur. The Gardner grading correction also demonstrates guideline knowledge.

Recommendations are highly specific and practical: immediate smoking cessation framed as the top priority, alcohol cessation from transfer onward, single embryo transfer rationale, fresh vs frozen transfer decision framework with specific hormonal criteria, structured post-failure workup sequence (embryo cohort review, uterine assessment, endometriosis-focused planning, PGT-A discussion), and explicit guidance on what NOT to do prematurely. The offer to provide a clinic-style counseling note or numerical outcome breakdown adds further practical value.
